transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-12-02
Start: 16:00 UTC
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Lena Ortiz (Redwood AE), Marcus Hwang (Redwood SE), David Chen (Monarch - Head of IT Risk), Amira Khatib (Monarch - Security Manager), Paul Ramos (Monarch - Procurement)

Auto-generated summary: quick walkthrough of SIG/CAIQ items; requests for SOC2 report, pen test evidence, KMS diagrams; next steps and evidence upload.

[00:00] Lena Ortiz: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, um quick intro, I'm Lena AE at Redwood, with Marcus our SE.
[00:10] David Chen: Hi all, David here, lead on IT risk, thanks.
[00:15] Amira Khatib: Amira, security. Paul from procurement is on.
[00:20] Paul Ramos: yep thanks for having us.
[00:25] Marcus Hwang: great, we'll kick off, the goal for today is to walk through the core SIG sections you flagged — encryption, keys, audit logging, SSO and RBAC, and any evidence requests so you know what's possible on our side.

[00:45] Lena Ortiz: Quick callouts — Redwood offers hosted API, Dedicated and Private deployments, so tell us if you want VPC/on-prem specifics.
[00:52] David Chen: Monarch is primarily interested in Dedicated or Private, we need region isolation and strict audit trails. SOC 2 and possibly ISO questions too.

[01:10] Marcus Hwang: Ok sounds good. Starting with SOC2 — we have a SOC 2 Type II for 2025-01 to 2026-01, and we can share the full report under an NDA / secure link. Pen test summary and remediation evidence we can also provide.
[01:30] Amira Khatib: great. for SIG question A.2.2 we need the actual report and the auditor firm name. also evidence of patching cadence.
[01:40] Lena Ortiz: we'll upload the report and the auditor info. patching cadence — Marcus, do you want to cover how we handle infra patching for hosted and dedicated?

[01:55] Marcus Hwang: sure, for hosted our infra is managed with a rolling patch schedule, weekly critical updates, monthly maintenance windows. For Dedicated we provide control plane ops but customers can opt into our managed patching. I'll pull the ops runbook snippet and the maintenance calendar screenshot.

[02:20] David Chen: and for private deployments, we need to know if keys can be customer-managed. BYOK?
[02:27] Marcus Hwang: yes, we support BYOK for Private and Dedicated via KMS integrations and HSM-backed keys on request. For hosted there is a Redwood-managed KMS; we also offer an option to integrate customer's cloud KMS for dedicated/private. I'll share the KMS architecture doc.

[02:50] Amira Khatib: encryption at rest/encryption in transit — are TLS and AES-256 used? any note on cert rotation?
[02:58] Marcus Hwang: TLS 1.2+ enforced, ASN cert rotation is automated, and data at rest uses AES-256; key rotation policies are configurable. We'll provide the key rotation schedule and where rotation logs live.

[03:20] Paul Ramos: On the procurement side we need a timeline to get these docs into our vendor risk portal, ideally within a week.

[03:30] Lena Ortiz: understood — we'll aim to upload the SOC 2 and pen test summary within 3-4 business days.

[03:40] David Chen: Audit logging: do you capture admin activity, key access, and model inference logs? retention?

[03:48] Marcus Hwang: yes — we capture admin API actions, role changes, SSO events, and model call metadata (no full PII unless supplied). Retention defaults to 90 days for hosted but Dedicated/Private can extend; we can export logs to your SIEM (SPLUNK / S3) — would you like SIEM integration?

[04:15] Amira Khatib: we do use Splunk. ability to stream logs and long-term retention is required for audit. Also chain of custody for logs during incidents?

[04:25] Marcus Hwang: logs can be exported in append-only form to your S3 bucket, and we provide signed delivery for chain of custody. I'll add the Splunk forwarding config and an example of the audit log schema.

[04:45] David Chen: RBAC and SSO — we require SAML SSO, SCIM provisioning, and fine-grained roles. how mature is that?

[04:52] Lena Ortiz: Redwood supports SAML 2.0, OIDC, SCIM for provisioning, and we have role-based access controls with admin/observer/operator roles. Marcus can show the console screenshots.

[05:05] Marcus Hwang: console supports role templates and custom roles, plus MFA for admin accounts. SCIM sync supports group mapping — we'll send screenshots and a SCIM attribute guide.

[05:20] Amira Khatib: for SIG there is a few items on privileged access reviews and separation of duties — do you have a documented process?

[05:28] Marcus Hwang: yes, privileged access is gated. we have a quarterly privileged access review and an approval workflow in the console. I will attach the policy excerpt and screenshots of the approval workflow.

[05:45] David Chen: data residency — Monarch requires primary data to remain in eu-west-1 for EU customers. How do you ensure region residency for logs and model context?

[05:55] Marcus Hwang: we can pin workloads to eu-west-1 for Dedicated/Private and for Hosted we can enable regional routing with a data residency agreement. logs and backups for pinned workloads stay in the selected region; I'll include our data residency whitepaper and the routing policy doc.

[06:15] Paul Ramos: any third-party subprocessors we need to note on SIG?

[06:20] Lena Ortiz: yes, we list subprocessors in our security addendum; common ones are cloud provider (AWS/GCP), monitoring vendor, and our CDNs. we'll produce the current subprocessors list and contact info.

[06:35] Marcus Hwang: also note we use a limited set of vendor tools for telemetry; we can provide ATOs and SOC reports where available.

[06:45] Amira Khatib: CAIQ vs SIG — we were asked to collect both; which is easier?

[06:50] Lena Ortiz: SIG is preferred for banking procurement; CAIQ overlap is high. we can pre-fill a SIG worksheet for you and highlight areas that need evidence.

[07:05] David Chen: great. evidence: SOC 2, pen test, KMS diagrams, patching runbook, RBAC screenshots, SCIM config, and subprocessors list. any sample artifacts for encryption key access logs?

[07:20] Marcus Hwang: yes i'll export sample key access logs (redacted) and a sample KMS event stream. note: real key ids will be redacted.

[07:35] Amira Khatib: about key custody — if we want BYOK and the keys in our KMS, do you support HSM-backed keys and separate split custody?

[07:42] Marcus Hwang: yes, HSM-backed keys via Cloud HSM or customer HSM for private deployments. split custody workflows can be discussed in the deep-dive; I'll bring our security architect.

[08:00] Paul Ramos: procurement wants any standard PO terms and the data processing agreement; also SLAs.

[08:08] Lena Ortiz: we'll attach our standard DPA and SLA in the secure share. For Dedicated contracts we can negotiate retention and SLAs.

[08:20] David Chen: do you maintain ISO 27001?

[08:24] Marcus Hwang: currently SOC 2 Type II; ISO 27001 in progress — we expect certification in H1 2027. we'll provide the status and scope doc.

[08:40] Amira Khatib: incident response — do you provide notifications, runbooks, and post-mortems?

[08:46] Marcus Hwang: yes, incident response playbooks, 24/7 on-call for enterprise tiers, notification timelines in the DPA; we'll attach a redacted post-mortem example.

[09:05] David Chen: ok that's helpful. a couple of SIG-specific Qs: can you map your controls to our internal control IDs?

[09:12] Lena Ortiz: we can produce a controls mapping spreadsheet to help Monarch map Redwood controls to their framework.

[09:20] Marcus Hwang: and for evidence upload we can either push to your vendor portal or provide secure SFTP/SharePoint links; which do you prefer?

[09:28] Paul Ramos: vendor portal is preferred, but SFTP is fine as a fallback. we need a file manifest.

[09:35] Lena Ortiz: we'll prepare a manifest with each artifact and link.

[09:42] Amira Khatib: one more: retention of inference data — do you keep prompt/response payloads by default?

[09:48] Marcus Hwang: default hosted retention is 30 days for request/response metadata; Dedicated/Private can configure not to retain or to forward to your storage. We also support configurable PII redaction at ingest via rules. I'll attach the data retention config docs.

[10:10] David Chen: good. any blockers to getting SIG done in a week?

[10:15] Lena Ortiz: none from our side; we'll get the primary artifacts uploaded, and Marcus will follow up on technical docs.

[10:22] Marcus Hwang: I'll schedule the deep dive with the Monarch infra team — likely 60-90 minute session. tentative week of 2026-12-08.

[10:30] Paul Ramos: procurement will follow up after we receive the docs.

[10:35] Lena Ortiz: recap: we'll upload SOC2 + pen test + subprocessors + RBAC/SCIM screenshots + KMS diagrams + audit log examples. Monarch will finish SIG subset and confirm whether they want Hosted or Dedicated for pilot.

[10:50] David Chen: thanks, appreciate it.

[10:55] Amira Khatib: thanks all.

[11:00] Lena Ortiz: thanks everyone — we'll send a calendar invite for the deep technical session and the SFTP link for upload.

End of call.
